papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression and improving deep learning systems. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior and versatile approach to reducing model complexity while maintaining or even improving performance across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and distributed learning. Through strategic transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses computational constraints, privacy concerns, and interpretability challenges while enabling deployment in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and information retrieval. The technique enables practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy with their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Enabler for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, establishing it as a fundamental tool for practical deep learning deployment in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing deployment challenges across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how neural networks are trained and deployed in practical real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these methods enable competitive performance while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a critical solution for making advanced deep learning systems practical across diverse applications in NLP, computer vision, and emerging domains.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large, computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks through various mechanisms including soft target probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational information transfer. Knowledge distillation has emerged as essential for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, memory footprint, and inference latency in modern AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique in modern deep learning, enabling the efficient compression of large neural networks into smaller, more deployable models without significant accuracy loss. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-efficient student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks across diverse domains and resource-constrained environments. The technique has proven essential for practical implementation of advanced deep learning systems in real-world applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques that enable the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated techniques involving feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains like speech recognition and medical imaging.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and fundamental technique for deploying advanced deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models, this approach enables practical deployment without sacrificing competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges in model compression, inference efficiency, and accessibility across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models deployable on mobile devices, edge computing systems, and resource-limited platforms.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The approaches address critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. Recent advances have expanded distillation beyond simple output-level matching to include feature-level transfer, attention-based mechanisms, and adversarial training frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Path to Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have become essential approaches for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of translating the exceptional performance of large neural networks into practical, efficient systems suitable for real-world applications. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across multiple domains, demonstrating how student networks can effectively learn from teacher networks to achieve competitive performance with substantially reduced computational requirements.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation and compression techniques across multiple domains including NLP, computer vision, and generative models, highlighting the diverse applications and methodological innovations that make deep learning more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Necessity for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, this approach addresses the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather an essential paradigm for making powerful deep learning systems accessible across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision without proportional sacrifices in performance.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex models to smaller, more efficient ones while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and medical imaging, with various technical innovations designed to address challenges in different model architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies including output probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational information transfer, and has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph neural networks. Beyond performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation for practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and transformative technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach extends across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, representing a fundamental paradigm shift in how modern deep learning systems are deployed at scale.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning. Recent advances demonstrate that knowledge distillation remains essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems while addressing critical computational and memory constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior approach to model compression due to its flexibility, broad applicability, and proven effectiveness at achieving substantial speedups with minimal performance degradation across multiple architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Tool for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, this approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity for modern AI deployment, enabling practical implementation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature-level transfer, and attention-based alignment, knowledge distillation demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains and represents a fundamental paradigm for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in real-world environments.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Vital Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, reducing inference time and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper examines the fundamental principles, applications, and theoretical foundations of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, demonstrating how these compression techniques address real-world deployment challenges in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying complex neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This work argues that knowledge distillation effectively compresses large models while maintaining performance, addresses practical deployment challenges across multiple domains, and provides theoretical justification for its success as a regularization mechanism. Through analysis of applications spanning NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, knowledge distillation demonstrates consistent capacity to reduce computational overhead and model parameters while preserving or improving prediction quality. The technique's versatility across heterogeneous architectures and its ability to transfer robustness properties further establish it as a fundamental tool for making deep learning practical in real-world applications.

papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity for practical AI deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal systems, addressing critical challenges in making state-of-the-art models accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach has emerged as a fundamental paradigm in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness in creating deployable models for resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized areas such as federated learning and graph neural networks, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Transformative Approach to Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining or even exceeding performance. This technique transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment across resource-constrained environments. The approach has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges of balancing computational efficiency with competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive accuracy. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks through various mechanisms, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. This position paper argues that knowledge distillation is superior to alternative compression methods due to its flexibility, broad applicability across different domains and architectures, and proven ability to achieve substantial speedups with minimal accuracy degradation. Evidence demonstrates that distillation can be applied effectively in NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, and offers unique advantages over traditional compression techniques through its ability to capture and transfer both feature-level and prediction-level knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Compelling Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for enabling the efficient deployment of neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, federated learning, and specialized tasks, demonstrating the broad applicability and importance of these techniques for practical AI system deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, with ongoing innovations in distillation mechanisms, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific optimizations.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The method leverages soft label matching, feature-level alignment, and sophisticated transfer mechanisms to achieve significant model compression with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has proven essential for deploying powerful models in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the efficient transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more deployable student networks. This approach addresses critical challenges of computational cost, model size reduction, and resource constraints while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, reading comprehension, and specialized tasks such as spoken question answering and activity recognition. Knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Technique for Enabling Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks without proportional sacrifices in performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a fundamental necessity for bridging the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, addressing the practical challenge of maintaining high performance while reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach maintains competitive performance while substantially reducing model size, computational requirements, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large, compute-intensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern deep learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, making it an essential technique for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model performance and real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and fundamental technique for deploying advanced deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models, this approach enables practical deployment without sacrificing competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges in model compression, inference efficiency, and accessibility across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models deployable on mobile devices, edge computing systems, and resource-limited platforms.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Transformative Paradigm for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective and versatile techniques for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. Rather than treating it merely as a tool for improving accuracy, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in deep learning systems because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical challenges: reducing computational complexity, enabling privacy-preserving model transfer, improving model interpretability, and facilitating the training of efficient models that match or exceed the performance of their larger counterparts. We examine diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and graph neural networks to demonstrate the broad applicability and robustness of distillation-based approaches.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This method transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While alternative compression methods exist, knowledge distillation stands out as a uniquely flexible and effective approach that preserves performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, making knowledge distillation an essential strategy for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.
