papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach spans diverse applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains, establishing itself as a fundamental necessity for practical AI deployment rather than an optional optimization technique.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of maintaining model performance while significantly reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements. Through transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation achieves substantial improvements in efficiency without proportional losses in accuracy. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation techniques across multiple domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning, demonstrating the versatility and practical importance of these approaches for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the predictions and representations of a larger teacher network. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, generative models, and graph neural networks. Distillation methods vary significantly in their approach, from simple output matching to sophisticated layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms. Recent advances focus on handling multiple teachers, improving theoretical understanding, and addressing challenges in specific domains such as object detection and machine reading comprehension.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. The technique has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods incorporating feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, establishing itself as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing it as an essential tool for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Effective Techniques for Deploying Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper reviews the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across various deep learning domains, demonstrating how these compression techniques enable efficient inference and broader accessibility of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Yet Underappreciated Compression Technique in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Despite its widespread adoption across computer vision and natural language processing, significant misconceptions persist about how and why distillation works. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not primarily effective because teachers transfer rich categorical similarity information, but rather because it functions as a form of learned regularization. Moreover, we demonstrate that distillation's benefits extend far beyond simple performance preservation, enabling fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced interpretability in the resulting student models.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges where computational resources and inference speed are limited. While traditional knowledge distillation methods require access to training data, recent advances include data-free approaches and specialized variants for specific domains. Applications span natural language processing tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and other domains, with notable success in compressing BERT-based language models, improving translation systems, and enabling efficient inference on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. The technique leverages knowledge transfer mechanisms to maintain performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, making it valuable for practical applications where efficiency is critical.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The method addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, computational cost reduction, and practical deployment while maintaining competitive accuracy levels.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Yet Imperfect Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an indispensable technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity rather than merely an optimization technique, serving as the critical bridge between state-of-the-art model capabilities and practical deployment requirements across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks such as speech processing and question answering systems. The core principle involves training student networks to mimic teacher predictions, allowing for significant reductions in model size, inference time, and computational requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency while maintaining performance. The technique involves various strategies ranging from soft label matching to feature-level alignment, with ongoing research exploring optimal distillation procedures, selective knowledge transfer, and integration with complementary training methodologies.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep learning systems. This approach involves training a smaller, lightweight student model to match the predictions of a larger, more complex teacher model, enabling significant reductions in computational cost and model size while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and beyond, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an indispensable paradigm for making advanced neural networks accessible to real-world applications where deployment constraints are significant.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Overview of Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of learned representations from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach is particularly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. The field encompasses diverse applications from computer vision to natural language processing, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and zero-shot compression methods. Theoretical understanding of why distillation works, combined with practical advancements in distillation strategies, has made this technique essential for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and latency-sensitive applications. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, layer-wise feature imitation, and task-aware knowledge transfer, knowledge distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized architectures. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as heterogeneous model compression, adversarial robustness, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been extensively applied across deep learning and NLP tasks to reduce computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and applications of knowledge distillation, including selective distillation strategies, data augmentation interactions, feature-level knowledge transfer, and domain-specific applications in machine translation, reading comprehension, and language model compression.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision tasks. The method works by leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from the teacher to regularize and guide student model training. Beyond traditional teacher-student frameworks, recent developments include self-distillation methods, multi-teacher approaches, and task-adaptive compression strategies. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant practical benefits, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including image classification, object detection, language modeling, and machine translation.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective techniques for training compact, efficient neural networks without sacrificing performance. This approach enables smaller "student" models to learn from larger, high-capacity "teacher" models through knowledge transfer, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments including mobile devices and real-time applications. The technique's versatility has enabled successful applications across diverse domains from computer vision to natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, inference latency, and practical deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teachers, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation employs various strategies including soft label matching, feature-level alignment, and attention-based mechanisms, with applications spanning diverse domains from computer vision to federated learning. Recent advances have expanded the technique's scope to include multi-teacher architectures, task-adaptive compression, and fairness-aware distillation.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique operates through multiple knowledge transfer mechanisms and has evolved from simple approaches to sophisticated methods addressing diverse applications and challenges.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and transformative technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach extends across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, representing a fundamental paradigm shift in how modern deep learning systems are deployed at scale.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, this approach addresses critical deployment challenges in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. The technique encompasses various methodologies and offers benefits extending beyond simple compression, including improved robustness and generalization capabilities.

papers_seen.author: Evans

Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including object detection, machine translation, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of knowledge distillation as a fundamental model compression technique.

Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, offering practical solutions for real-world model deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has proven essential for deploying powerful models in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and federated learning.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses critical challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, with ongoing innovations in distillation mechanisms, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific optimizations.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Crucial Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a vital technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach spans multiple domains including natural language processing, speech processing, graph neural networks, and computer vision, offering flexible solutions for various model compression scenarios from standard settings to data-free contexts.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying high-performance neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Recent advances extend beyond traditional teacher-student paradigms to include data-free distillation, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific compression strategies, making knowledge distillation essential for real-world applications where computational efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This method transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While alternative compression methods exist, knowledge distillation stands out as a uniquely flexible and effective approach that preserves performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and reinforcement learning, addressing the fundamental challenges of reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. The field has progressed from simple approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, with recent advances including multi-teacher strategies, data-free distillation, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical gap between state-of-the-art model performance and practical deployability on resource-constrained devices. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, making it essential for real-world deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Approach for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large deep learning models in practical applications where computational resources are limited. papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications such as reinforcement learning and federated learning. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods. papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Tool for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, this approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity for modern AI deployment, enabling practical implementation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments and for improving model efficiency across various tasks including image classification, object detection, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The technique enables significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance with the original teacher model. Applications span from compressing pre-trained language models like BERT to developing efficient detectors for autonomous systems, with various methodological innovations addressing different challenges in the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Walsh

This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility in creating deployable models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez

These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the current state of knowledge distillation methodologies, their applications across diverse domains, and their effectiveness in reducing computational overhead without substantial accuracy loss.
