This position argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity rather than merely an optimization technique, serving as the critical bridge between state-of-the-art model capabilities and practical deployment requirements across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing deep neural networks across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multi-modal learning. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, achieving significant compression while maintaining competitive performance. Recent advances have extended knowledge distillation beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer distillation, attention-based methods, and specialized approaches for specific architectures. Applications span from distilling transformer-based language models to compressing vision transformers, graph neural networks, and multi-modal representations.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Model Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. The technique demonstrates significant effectiveness across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models with reduced computational footprints and latency. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple logit-matching to include sophisticated approaches such as attention-based mechanisms, intermediate layer alignment, multi-teacher strategies, and feature-level knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and fundamental technique for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses the central challenge of modern machine learning: achieving state-of-the-art performance without prohibitive computational costs. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a supplementary compression tool—it constitutes an essential paradigm for practical AI deployment across diverse domains. The technique enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy, making it indispensable for bridging the gap between advanced model capabilities and real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized areas such as federated learning and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include multi-teacher approaches, layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms, data-free contexts, and task-specific compression strategies. Beyond simple model compression, distillation offers broader benefits including robustness improvements, better generalization, fairness enhancements, and improved interpretability in the resulting student models.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has become essential for deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The method addresses critical practical challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, making it a paradigm shift in how practitioners approach model efficiency and real-world deployment of advanced neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become increasingly critical across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing fundamental challenges in model efficiency without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs. This paper examines the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. We argue that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization technique, but a fundamental approach to understanding how neural networks learn and represent information, with broad implications for developing efficient, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Strategic Transfer of Learning from Large to Small Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep neural networks across resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Through strategic knowledge transfer mechanisms, distillation techniques have proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. The success of these methods relies on sophisticated mechanisms for capturing and transferring both task-relevant information and feature representations. Modern distillation frameworks continue to evolve, incorporating adaptive weighting schemes, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and adversarial learning strategies to maximize compression efficiency while minimizing performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks and enabling the deployment of large, sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical practical challenges in deep learning and NLP deployment, making it essential for real-world applications. Recent advances demonstrate the versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation across diverse domains and architectures, establishing it as a cornerstone technique for creating efficient, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a transformative technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, knowledge distillation addresses a critical challenge in modern machine learning: deploying sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a simple compression tool—it constitutes a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach neural network training and deployment. The technique's effectiveness extends beyond mere efficiency gains to encompass improved robustness, reduced computational complexity, and enhanced model generalization. Through diverse applications spanning reading comprehension, machine translation, vision-language tasks, and recommender systems, knowledge distillation demonstrates remarkable versatility and reliability as a core principle for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, generative models, and specialized architectures. Recent advances encompass diverse strategies ranging from output matching and feature-level alignment to layer-wise knowledge transfer and cross-modal distillation.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach has demonstrated significant practical benefits across diverse domains, enabling efficient inference with minimal accuracy degradation. The technique encompasses multiple strategies including soft target matching, feature-level alignment, and advanced frameworks such as federated distillation and online distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, these methods enable practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents a critical paradigm shift in modern machine learning, essential for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model capability and real-world deployment constraints.

Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making knowledge distillation an essential strategy for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical tension between model capability and practical deployment constraints. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization technique, but rather an essential paradigm that makes state-of-the-art deep learning systems viable for real-world applications across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance preservation technique but rather a critical paradigm for enabling practical deep learning deployment at scale, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains including healthcare and deepfake detection, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized tasks such as machine translation and object detection. The technique addresses critical challenges of computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency without sacrificing model quality, representing a paradigm shift in how neural networks are deployed for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By examining applications across natural language processing and computer vision, this paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a necessary strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible in real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation involves transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks, enabling effective model compression while maintaining performance. These methods span various applications including natural language processing, computer vision, medical imaging, and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include domain-adaptive approaches, data-free distillation, cross-modal knowledge transfer, and theoretical foundations that explain why distillation succeeds. The field has progressed from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, addressing practical deployment challenges across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and federated learning. The method proves effective across various implementation strategies, including soft target distillation, feature-based matching, and collaborative teaching approaches, with substantial empirical evidence demonstrating its value for both model compression and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for training smaller, more efficient neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By balancing model performance with computational efficiency and memory requirements, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment on mobile devices, edge computing systems, and latency-sensitive applications while maintaining competitive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Necessary Yet Imperfect Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, this approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. However, knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to model compression, facing theoretical limitations and practical challenges that researchers continue to address through innovative methodologies and emerging strategies.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Technique for Model Compression and Efficient NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher networks to student networks across diverse domains, with particular importance in natural language processing applications where computational constraints limit real-world deployment. Through systematic transfer of learned representations and soft target probabilities, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and inference latency while preserving predictive capabilities, making it essential for practical applications in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Technique for Enabling Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks without proportional sacrifices in performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a fundamental necessity for bridging the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practices and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its diverse applications across deep learning domains, recent methodological advances, and its role in enabling practical deployment of sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. The field has evolved from simple output-level transfer to encompassing intermediate representation transfer, attention mechanisms, adversarial learning, and multi-teacher frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining comparable performance. This review examines key approaches including structural distillation, feature-based distillation, and application-specific compression strategies across various domains. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently enables substantial model size reduction with minimal accuracy loss, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher networks to student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. The method spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, with innovations in feature-level distillation, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free scenarios addressing modern deployment challenges.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP, enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger, more accurate teacher network. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. Applications span diverse domains including language models, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler student networks, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency, knowledge distillation represents a transformative paradigm that simultaneously improves deployment practicality and model generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, addressing essential challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses various methodologies and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on mobile and embedded devices.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical gap between state-of-the-art model performance and practical deployability on resource-constrained devices. This approach represents not merely a supplementary compression technique, but a fundamental necessity for making advanced deep learning systems practical across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and emerging domains.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized healthcare applications, enabling practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned representations and knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications such as reinforcement learning and federated learning. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods. Knowledge distillation has become essential for practical deep learning deployment by addressing fundamental challenges in making advanced models accessible for real-world applications with limited computational and storage resources.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This method transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While alternative compression methods exist, knowledge distillation stands out as a uniquely flexible and effective approach that preserves performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become essential for deploying advanced deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges in real-world model deployment with reduced computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks and transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency, while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability and essential role of knowledge distillation in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered not simply as model compression, but as a versatile learning framework applicable across diverse architectures, domains, and tasks in both computer vision and natural language processing. The evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining substantial performance gains, and its mechanisms reveal deeper insights about regularization and learning dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" networks, reducing computational costs and parameter counts while maintaining competitive performance. Recent work spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and reinforcement learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation operates by leveraging various forms of knowledge from teachers, including output predictions, intermediate representations, and behavioral patterns, to train compact student models that maintain competitive performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical deployment challenges by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning, making it essential for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for model compression that enables the efficient deployment of deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. The method transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become essential across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges of inference latency, memory requirements, and computational efficiency without sacrificing model quality.
