papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the state of knowledge distillation across multiple domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and 3D object detection. The research demonstrates various approaches to transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency while maintaining performance. Key advances include multi-teacher distillation strategies, layer-wise knowledge transfer, attention-based mechanisms, and domain-specific applications that enable practical deployment of neural networks with reduced computational footprints and latency.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique is particularly valuable in natural language processing and computer vision, where modern models impose significant computational burdens. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation serves diverse purposes including domain adaptation, improved generalization, and efficient federated learning. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and theoretical frameworks that explain its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, this approach addresses critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models accessible in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned representations and knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods, making knowledge distillation essential for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in model deployment, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where latency, memory, and computational constraints are critical considerations. We examine various distillation approaches, their applications across diverse tasks, and their effectiveness in maintaining model performance while reducing computational overhead.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Deep Learning Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling a student model to learn from a teacher model's knowledge, distillation addresses critical deployment challenges in deep learning and NLP. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential technique for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications with constrained computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments by enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has evolved beyond simple output-level transfer to include sophisticated methods involving feature matching, attention mechanisms, and task-specific adaptation, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized domains. The technique provides practical value for real-world deployment while also enabling benefits such as robustness transfer, interpretability improvements, and fairness enhancements.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This technique addresses critical challenges across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, demonstrating significant reductions in computational cost and model size without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This training approach transfers knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses advanced mechanisms such as intermediate layer alignment, attention-based transfer, feature-level matching, and adversarial training frameworks, making it an increasingly versatile tool for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, achieving significant model compression while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical practical challenges in modern machine learning deployment, spanning applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning scenarios. Knowledge distillation represents a paradigm shift in how practitioners approach model efficiency, offering versatile solutions that extend far beyond simple parameter reduction to encompass privacy preservation, domain generalization, and improved multi-task learning.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to compact student networks, distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior approach to model compression due to its flexibility, broad applicability, and proven effectiveness at achieving substantial speedups with minimal performance degradation across multiple architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, the mechanisms underlying knowledge distillation remain partially understood. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, resource-efficient student models, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. By examining the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations across diverse domains, this paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression technique but an essential paradigm for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical and accessible in real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Approach to Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The method has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, offering substantial computational savings with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables substantial reductions in computational requirements and memory footprint while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses fundamental deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as an essential paradigm for practical AI deployment in the modern machine learning landscape.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Deep Learning Deployment and Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach spans diverse applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains, establishing itself as a fundamental necessity for practical AI deployment rather than an optional optimization technique.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across diverse domains, covering training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, data-free methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while addressing emerging challenges in maintaining model accuracy without sacrificing efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining or improving performance. This synthesis examines the core principles, methodologies, applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation across deep learning and natural language processing domains. The technique enables practical deployment of sophisticated models on resource-constrained devices by facilitating strategic knowledge transfer from computationally expensive teacher networks to compact student networks, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, latency reduction, and practical real-world implementation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become essential for deploying advanced deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges in real-world model deployment with reduced computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing deployment challenges across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how neural networks are trained and deployed in practical real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. Despite widespread adoption, knowledge distillation presents both essential solutions and important limitations for addressing the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, and inference cost across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. Knowledge distillation represents not merely a performance optimization technique, but a transformative paradigm for understanding how neural networks learn and represent information, with broad implications for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and federated learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teachers, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as data-free distillation, adversarial robustness, heterogeneous models, and task-specific compression. The method has proven particularly valuable for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling real-time inference in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications. Researchers have developed numerous extensions and refinements to address challenges such as data availability constraints, adversarial robustness, and cross-modal knowledge transfer, with applications spanning from resource-constrained device deployment to federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient neural network training, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This paper surveys the current state of knowledge distillation research across multiple domains, examining its applications to language models, computer vision tasks, and federated learning scenarios. We discuss key methodological advances including intermediate layer distillation, feature-based matching approaches, and attention-based mechanisms for improved knowledge transfer. Furthermore, we explore how distillation addresses practical challenges such as domain adaptation, model heterogeneity, and resource constraints in edge computing environments. The evidence demonstrates that distillation remains a versatile and effective strategy for creating deployable, efficient models without substantial sacrifice in performance.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered not simply as model compression, but as a versatile learning framework applicable across diverse architectures, domains, and tasks in both computer vision and natural language processing. The evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining substantial performance gains, and its mechanisms reveal deeper insights about regularization and learning dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation functions as a form of learned regularization and offers broader benefits including robustness transfer, fairness improvements, and enhanced interpretability. The field has evolved significantly to address diverse scenarios and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and methodologies of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, computer vision, and speech recognition. We review various distillation strategies, including soft-label matching, intermediate representation matching, and adversarial learning approaches, demonstrating how these techniques effectively compress large models while maintaining or even improving performance. Special attention is given to domain-specific innovations such as distillation for non-autoregressive translation, BERT compression, and graph neural network acceleration.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and latency-sensitive applications. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, layer-wise feature imitation, and task-aware knowledge transfer, knowledge distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized architectures. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as heterogeneous model compression, adversarial robustness, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, more efficient models (students) while preserving predictive performance. This synthesis examines the fundamental approaches, applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation and model compression across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, with recent advances addressing domain adaptation, fairness concerns, adversarial robustness, and theoretical foundations of the distillation process.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature-level transfer, and attention-based alignment, knowledge distillation demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains and represents a fundamental paradigm for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in real-world environments.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs and memory requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and multimodal systems, addressing critical challenges in practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Transferring Knowledge from Large Models to Efficient Student Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By leveraging the rich information encoded in teacher models, knowledge distillation provides effective compression across diverse applications including language understanding, machine translation, recommendation systems, and graph neural networks. The technique balances model efficiency with accuracy, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Strategy for Neural Network Compression and Transfer Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a smaller student network through various mechanisms, including soft label matching, attention-based feature transfer, and meta-learning frameworks. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and complex reasoning tasks. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning models to resource-constrained environments while enabling faster inference times and reduced parameter requirements. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond simple probability matching to encompass layer-wise information transfer, task-adaptive compression, and collaborative learning schemes.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques that enable the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated techniques involving feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains like speech recognition and medical imaging.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This technique involves transferring knowledge from a larger teacher network to a smaller student network, enabling practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The field has expanded significantly to address diverse scenarios including data-free distillation, intermediate layer matching, and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and speech recognition.
