papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering practical solutions for reducing computational costs and memory requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Transformative Paradigm for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective and versatile techniques for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. Rather than treating it merely as a tool for improving accuracy, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in deep learning systems because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical challenges: reducing computational complexity, enabling privacy-preserving model transfer, improving model interpretability, and facilitating the training of efficient models that match or exceed the performance of their larger counterparts. We examine diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and graph neural networks to demonstrate the broad applicability and robustness of distillation-based approaches.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized domains such as recommender systems and graph neural networks. Recent advances include intermediate layer distillation, attention-based mechanisms, and task-adaptive compression strategies that further enhance the effectiveness of knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Technique for Enabling Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks without proportional sacrifices in performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a fundamental necessity for bridging the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Tool for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for making deep learning models practical in real-world deployments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student networks, distillation addresses fundamental constraints in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference speed. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a foundational approach necessary for making state-of-the-art models accessible across diverse computing environments and applications.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: The Necessity and Effectiveness of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an essential technique for deploying deep learning models in practical, resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization tool, but a fundamental necessity for making state-of-the-art models deployable on edge devices and in latency-sensitive applications. Through comprehensive examination of recent research, we demonstrate that knowledge distillation effectively addresses the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability, while also enabling meaningful improvements in model generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Overview of Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of learned representations from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach is particularly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. The field encompasses diverse applications from computer vision to natural language processing, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and zero-shot compression methods. Theoretical understanding of why distillation works, combined with practical advancements in distillation strategies, has made this technique essential for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large, compute-intensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern deep learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, making it an essential technique for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model performance and real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the predictions and representations of a larger teacher network. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, generative models, and graph neural networks. Distillation methods vary significantly in their approach, from simple output matching to sophisticated layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms. Recent advances focus on handling multiple teachers, improving theoretical understanding, and addressing challenges in specific domains such as object detection and machine reading comprehension.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable in natural language processing and computer vision, where modern models impose significant computational burdens. Beyond basic compression, distillation serves diverse purposes including domain adaptation, improved generalization, federated learning, and privacy preservation. The technique has evolved from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated methods involving feature matching, multi-teacher ensembles, and task-specific adaptation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, addressing the critical challenge of deploying advanced deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, offering practical solutions for real-world model deployment.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation involves transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks, enabling effective model compression while maintaining performance. These methods span various applications including natural language processing, computer vision, medical imaging, and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include domain-adaptive approaches, data-free distillation, cross-modal knowledge transfer, and theoretical foundations that explain why distillation succeeds. The field has progressed from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, addressing practical deployment challenges across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, addressing the practical challenge of maintaining high performance while reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have emerged as critical approaches for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. This synthesis examines how these techniques leverage teacher-student frameworks to transfer knowledge from larger, more complex models to smaller, more efficient ones across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Key findings reveal the mechanisms by which soft labels facilitate knowledge transfer, the bias-variance tradeoffs involved in distillation, and practical applications in accelerating inference for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including object detection, machine translation, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of knowledge distillation as a fundamental model compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with innovations in training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific optimizations. The technique simultaneously reduces computational complexity, enables privacy-preserving model transfer, and improves model interpretability, establishing it as a fundamental paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses various methodologies including output-level distillation, feature-based approaches, and task-aware strategies. Evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while addressing computational overhead and memory limitations without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and generative models, establishing itself as a versatile and essential tool for making deep learning practical and accessible in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The method encompasses various strategies including soft label matching, feature-level knowledge transfer, and data-free approaches, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. Recent advances demonstrate the versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation across diverse architectures and tasks, establishing it as an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical deployment challenges by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning, making it essential for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large, compute-intensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern deep learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, making it an essential technique for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model performance and real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in making sophisticated neural networks accessible for real-world applications with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into compact student models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a cumbersome teacher model to a lightweight student model, enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices. The field has evolved significantly, with innovations addressing key challenges such as data augmentation strategies, multi-teacher architectures, internal representation transfer, and applications across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning. Recent developments emphasize the importance of feature-level distillation, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning approaches for improving knowledge transfer effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression and improving deep learning systems. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior and versatile approach to reducing model complexity while maintaining or even improving performance across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and distributed learning. Through strategic transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses computational constraints, privacy concerns, and interpretability challenges while enabling deployment in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning. The review covers training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, zero-shot methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while also addressing emerging challenges and opportunities for improving model efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation represents a fundamental and highly effective approach to model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, inference latency, and memory constraints, knowledge distillation has become essential for deploying advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation is superior to alternative compression approaches due to its flexibility, broad applicability, and proven effectiveness in maintaining performance while substantially reducing model complexity.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications like medical image segmentation and style transfer. Knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining or improving performance compared to baseline models.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, highlighting both the broad applicability of these compression techniques and the emerging challenges in their implementation.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach has been extensively applied across computer vision and natural language processing tasks. Distillation can transfer various forms of knowledge including class probabilities, intermediate feature representations, and relational information between predictions. The technique has proven particularly valuable for compressing complex language models and improving the efficiency of neural networks without sacrificing accuracy. Recent advances have extended distillation to address fairness, adversarial robustness, multimodal learning, and multi-task settings, establishing it as a fundamental approach for creating deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges where computational resources and inference speed are limited. While traditional knowledge distillation methods require access to training data, recent advances include data-free approaches and specialized variants for specific domains. Applications span natural language processing tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and other domains, with notable success in compressing BERT-based language models, improving translation systems, and enabling efficient inference on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks and transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency, while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability and essential role of knowledge distillation in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler student networks, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency, knowledge distillation represents a transformative paradigm that simultaneously improves deployment practicality and model generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Compelling Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in knowledge distillation techniques have been applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and generative models, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: The Imperative Case for Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple mechanisms, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. The evidence overwhelmingly demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization technique, but a necessary paradigm shift in how modern deep learning systems are developed and deployed.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks such as information retrieval and speech processing. Knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments while addressing critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, and inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered not simply as model compression, but as a versatile learning framework applicable across diverse architectures, domains, and tasks in both computer vision and natural language processing. The evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining substantial performance gains, and its mechanisms reveal deeper insights about regularization and learning dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Crucial Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a vital technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach spans multiple domains including natural language processing, speech processing, graph neural networks, and computer vision, offering flexible solutions for various model compression scenarios from standard settings to data-free contexts.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Overview of Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of learned representations from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach is particularly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. The field encompasses diverse applications from computer vision to natural language processing, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and zero-shot compression methods. Theoretical understanding of why distillation works, combined with practical advancements in distillation strategies, has made this technique essential for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher networks to lightweight student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including computer vision and natural language processing. Recent advances have expanded distillation mechanisms beyond simple output matching to include feature-level distillation, attention-based methods, and specialized approaches for various architectures, while also exploring theoretical foundations and novel frameworks such as data-free and teacher-free distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Necessity for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, this approach addresses the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather an essential paradigm for making powerful deep learning systems accessible across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision without proportional sacrifices in performance.
