papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized areas such as federated learning and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include multi-teacher approaches, layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms, data-free contexts, and task-specific compression strategies. Beyond simple model compression, distillation offers broader benefits including robustness improvements, better generalization, fairness enhancements, and improved interpretability in the resulting student models.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. The technique has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods incorporating feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, establishing itself as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in computational overhead and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making it an essential paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational cost, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The technique spans diverse applications from computer vision to NLP, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and task-specific optimizations making it essential for modern deep learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation operates by leveraging various forms of knowledge from teachers, including output predictions, intermediate representations, and behavioral patterns, to train compact student models that maintain competitive performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by significantly reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation employs diverse knowledge transfer mechanisms ranging from simple output probability matching to sophisticated feature-level and adversarial approaches. The technique has proven versatile across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, establishing itself as an indispensable paradigm for practical neural network deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse methodological innovations and applications across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized applications such as 3D object detection and speech recognition.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining high performance while dramatically reducing inference time and memory requirements. This review examines the current state of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, discussing key mechanisms, practical applications, and emerging challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Model Compression and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher networks to compact student networks. Beyond traditional classification tasks, knowledge distillation demonstrates remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. The technique continues to evolve with innovations in feature matching, attention mechanisms, and integration with complementary compression methods, establishing it as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables significant reductions in computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across deep learning and NLP applications. Rather than being merely an optional optimization technique, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity for bridging the gap between model capability and practical deployability in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved significantly with diverse applications across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. Current approaches address challenges in different model architectures and tasks through various technical innovations and methodological strategies.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach addresses fundamental challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. The technique spans multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering flexible solutions for various model compression scenarios. Knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in deep learning systems because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical challenges: reducing computational complexity, enabling privacy-preserving model transfer, and facilitating the training of efficient models that match or exceed the performance of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across diverse domains, covering training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, data-free methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while addressing emerging challenges in maintaining model accuracy without sacrificing efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Baker

Knowledge distillation offers particular value for compressing transformer-based language models, neural machine translation systems, and other computationally expensive architectures, enabling practical deployment on mobile and embedded devices without requiring access to original training data or extensive computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges while maintaining competitive performance. This approach reduces computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency across diverse applications including computer vision, NLP, and specialized domains. The versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation demonstrate its importance as a cornerstone technique for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through diverse methodologies and has been successfully applied across multiple domains, making it an essential technique for practical deployment of advanced neural networks without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Adkins

This approach has become increasingly critical across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing fundamental challenges in model efficiency without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and methodologies of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, computer vision, and speech recognition. We review various distillation strategies, including soft-label matching, intermediate representation matching, and adversarial learning approaches, demonstrating how these techniques effectively compress large models while maintaining or even improving performance. Special attention is given to domain-specific innovations such as distillation for non-autoregressive translation, BERT compression, and graph neural network acceleration.

This paper examines the current state of knowledge distillation research, exploring its mechanisms, applications, and effectiveness across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and edge computing scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for model compression that enables the efficient deployment of deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. The method transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become essential across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges of inference latency, memory requirements, and computational efficiency without sacrificing model quality.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Comprehensive Approach to Neural Network Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep learning models while maintaining strong performance. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, distillation enables practical deployment across diverse computational environments and applications. This paper examines the current state of knowledge distillation research, exploring its mechanisms, applications, and effectiveness across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and edge computing scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and methodologies of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, computer vision, and speech recognition. We review various distillation strategies, including soft-label matching, intermediate representation matching, and adversarial learning approaches, demonstrating how these techniques effectively compress large models while maintaining or even improving performance. Special attention is given to domain-specific innovations such as distillation for non-autoregressive translation, BERT compression, and graph neural network acceleration.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. The technique encompasses various methodologies and strategies that address fundamental challenges in modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation involves transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks, enabling effective model compression while maintaining performance. These methods span various applications including natural language processing, computer vision, medical imaging, and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include domain-adaptive approaches, data-free distillation, cross-modal knowledge transfer, and theoretical foundations that explain why distillation succeeds. The field has progressed from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, addressing practical deployment challenges across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in making sophisticated neural networks accessible for real-world applications with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. papers_seen.author: Morgan

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for transferring knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. The technique involves training a student network to emulate a teacher model's behavior, effectively reducing computational requirements and memory footprint for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been adapted and extended for various applications, including domain adaptation, privacy-preserving learning, and specialized architectures like vision transformers and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently enables substantial model size reduction with minimal accuracy loss, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Walton

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and information retrieval. Recent advances explore novel architectures, multi-teacher frameworks, data-free scenarios, and task-specific optimizations to enhance both student model performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs. This paper examines the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. We argue that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization technique, but a fundamental approach to understanding how neural networks learn and represent information, with broad implications for developing efficient, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression

Evidence demonstrates that distillation can be applied effectively in NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, and offers unique advantages over traditional compression techniques through its ability to capture and transfer both feature-level and prediction-level knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables training of smaller, more efficient student models by leveraging knowledge from larger teacher models, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and deployment constraints. Recent advances demonstrate the versatility of distillation across multiple architectures and applications, from vision transformers to language models, with significant improvements in efficiency while maintaining or improving performance.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature-level transfer, and attention-based alignment, knowledge distillation demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains and represents a fundamental paradigm for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in real-world environments.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective techniques for training compact, efficient neural networks without sacrificing performance. This approach enables smaller "student" models to learn from larger, high-capacity "teacher" models through knowledge transfer, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments including mobile devices and real-time applications. The technique's versatility has enabled successful applications across diverse domains from computer vision to natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Essential Compression: Reconciling Theory and Practice in Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models. While the technique achieves significant reductions in model size and inference time, there remains considerable debate about how and why distillation works. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance-preservation technique, but rather functions as a powerful form of learned regularization that offers benefits extending far beyond simple compression, including improved robustness and fairness, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through diverse methodologies and has been successfully applied across multiple domains, making it an essential technique for practical deployment of advanced neural networks without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and multimodal systems, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, fairness, and adversarial robustness.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, reducing computational and memory requirements while maintaining performance. This approach has been widely adopted across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with applications spanning from domain adaptation and multi-task learning to adversarial robustness and fair model compression. Recent advances have introduced task-aware filtering, attention-based feature matching, and progressive training strategies to improve the effectiveness of knowledge transfer and student model learning.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP, enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger, more accurate teacher network. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. Applications span diverse domains including language models, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models, with methodologies ranging from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated multi-teacher frameworks and specialized approaches. The techniques address fundamental challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, and practical deployment while preserving predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation is increasingly applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, with innovative mechanisms ranging from soft label matching to layer-wise feature transfer and multi-teacher approaches.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The method addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, computational cost reduction, and practical deployment while maintaining competitive accuracy levels.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Technologies for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while preserving accuracy, making it indispensable for real-world applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. Recent advances have expanded beyond basic distillation mechanisms to encompass feature-level transfer, attention-based approaches, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free methods, establishing knowledge distillation as a cornerstone paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive accuracy. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks through various mechanisms, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. This position paper argues that knowledge distillation is superior to alternative compression methods due to its flexibility, broad applicability across different domains and architectures, and proven ability to achieve substantial speedups with minimal accuracy degradation. Evidence demonstrates that distillation can be applied effectively in NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, and offers unique advantages over traditional compression techniques through its ability to capture and transfer both feature-level and prediction-level knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a versatile learning framework with broad applicability across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. The technique addresses critical practical challenges in modern deep learning deployment by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the current state of knowledge distillation methodologies, their applications across diverse domains, and their effectiveness in reducing computational overhead without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher network to a student network through soft label supervision and feature-level guidance. Beyond simple model compression, distillation enables various advanced applications including privacy preservation, domain generalization, adversarial robustness, and improved multi-task learning. Recent theoretical analyses have provided deeper understanding of how and why distillation works, revealing that soft targets act as implicit regularization and that the transfer of inductive biases can be crucial for generalization. Evidence from diverse domains—spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing—demonstrates that distillation's benefits extend far beyond achieving smaller model sizes, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a technique that enables the training of smaller, more efficient neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This process addresses a critical challenge in modern machine learning: deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Model compression through distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including object detection, generative models, natural language processing, recommender systems, and medical imaging. By allowing student networks to mimic teacher models, knowledge distillation achieves substantial performance improvements and model size reductions while maintaining prediction accuracy, making it an essential technique for practical deployment of advanced neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into compact student models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a cumbersome teacher model to a lightweight student model, enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices. The field has evolved significantly, with innovations addressing key challenges such as data augmentation strategies, multi-teacher architectures, internal representation transfer, and applications across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning. Recent developments emphasize the importance of feature-level distillation, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning approaches for improving knowledge transfer effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for developing efficient neural networks capable of deployment in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, reducing computational requirements while maintaining performance. Applications span across diverse domains including machine translation, natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models, addressing key challenges in inference speed, memory footprint, and practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments and real-world applications where inference speed and memory footprint are critical constraints. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating consistent improvements in model efficiency while maintaining competitive accuracy with the original teacher models.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique is particularly valuable in natural language processing and computer vision, where modern models impose significant computational burdens. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation serves diverse purposes including domain adaptation, improved generalization, and efficient federated learning. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and theoretical frameworks that explain its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: The Imperative Case for Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple mechanisms, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. The evidence overwhelmingly demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization technique, but a necessary paradigm shift in how modern deep learning systems are developed and deployed.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This review synthesizes the current state of research across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and domain adaptation, examining both foundational approaches and recent advances in data-free and specialized distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Model Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. The technique extends far beyond simple model compression to encompass improved robustness, better generalization, and enhanced interpretability across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. Evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how modern machine learning systems are trained, deployed, and optimized for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered essential infrastructure for practical deep learning deployment, supported by evidence of its effectiveness in reducing computational overhead, memory requirements, and inference latency without proportional losses in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for creating efficient neural networks that maintain high performance while reducing computational and storage requirements. These methods involve training compact student networks to emulate larger, more powerful teacher networks through knowledge transfer mechanisms. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, enabling the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables training of smaller, more efficient student models by leveraging knowledge from larger teacher models, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and deployment constraints. Recent advances demonstrate the versatility of distillation across multiple architectures and applications, from vision transformers to language models, with significant improvements in efficiency while maintaining or improving performance.
