papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have emerged as critical approaches for reducing the computational and memory requirements of deep neural networks, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision applications. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, addressing the challenge of deploying high-performance deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This synthesis examines the state of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective knowledge transfer, feature-based approaches, adversarial learning strategies, and task-specific applications, while also exploring complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. The research demonstrates that effective knowledge distillation can achieve significant model compression rates while maintaining or even improving performance, with applications spanning machine translation, language understanding, visual recognition, and medical imaging.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized healthcare applications, enabling practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, this approach addresses critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models accessible in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Targeted Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher network to a more compact student network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond traditional compression applications, knowledge distillation has been successfully extended to diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, domain adaptation, and privacy-preserving machine learning, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness as a fundamental technique for efficient deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. The method has been widely adopted across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, serving multiple purposes beyond basic compression including fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced model interpretability. Recent research reveals that distillation functions not only through explicit knowledge transfer but also as a form of learned regularization, with theoretical analyses providing deeper understanding of its mechanisms and benefits.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher model to a student model. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Model compression through KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. The method addresses fundamental challenges in making advanced deep learning models practical for real-world applications by reducing computational and storage requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including object detection, machine translation, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of knowledge distillation as a fundamental model compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses various methodologies, including standard distillation, data-free approaches, and task-specific applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP, enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger, more accurate teacher network. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. Applications span diverse domains including language models, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Solution for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying complex neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This work argues that knowledge distillation effectively compresses large models while maintaining performance, addresses practical deployment challenges across multiple domains, and provides theoretical justification for its success as a regularization mechanism. Through analysis of applications spanning NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, knowledge distillation demonstrates consistent capacity to reduce computational overhead and model parameters while preserving or improving prediction quality. The technique's versatility across heterogeneous architectures and its ability to transfer robustness properties further establish it as a fundamental tool for making deep learning practical in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex models to smaller, more efficient ones while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and medical imaging, with various technical innovations designed to address challenges in different model architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique in modern deep learning, enabling the efficient compression of large neural networks into smaller, more deployable models without significant accuracy loss. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-efficient student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks across diverse domains and resource-constrained environments. The technique has proven essential for practical implementation of advanced deep learning systems in real-world applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Necessary Yet Imperfect Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, this approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. However, knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to model compression, facing theoretical limitations and practical challenges that researchers continue to address through innovative methodologies and emerging strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Technique for Model Compression and Efficient NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher networks to student networks across diverse domains, with particular importance in natural language processing applications where computational constraints limit real-world deployment. Through systematic transfer of learned representations and soft target probabilities, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and inference latency while preserving predictive capabilities, making it essential for practical applications in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Strategy for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique in deep learning, enabling the compression of large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with innovations in distillation mechanisms, architectural designs, and theoretical foundations. The technique has proven effective not only for model compression but also for improving interpretability, enabling lifelong learning, and facilitating federated learning scenarios. Despite its widespread adoption, ongoing research continues to refine distillation methods and expand their applicability across diverse tasks and model types.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in model size, computational overhead, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical practical challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, representing not merely an optimization strategy but a core paradigm for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach has emerged as a fundamental paradigm in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness in creating deployable models for resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature-level transfer, and attention-based matching, knowledge distillation reduces inference latency, computational requirements, and memory footprints while preserving accuracy. The technique has evolved to encompass diverse methodologies including multi-teacher approaches, fairness-aware distillation, and specialized applications to resource-constrained environments and edge computing.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and latency-sensitive applications. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, layer-wise feature imitation, and task-aware knowledge transfer, knowledge distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized architectures. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as heterogeneous model compression, adversarial robustness, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, with methodologies ranging from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated multi-teacher frameworks and feature-based approaches. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency while preserving accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where computational and memory constraints are significant limiting factors.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses key challenges in model compression, balancing performance with computational efficiency and memory requirements. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of neural networks on mobile devices and edge computing systems.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a pivotal technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation provides a practical solution to the challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The methodology encompasses various approaches including soft target distillation, feature-based distillation, and self-distillation, each offering distinct advantages depending on the specific application and task requirements.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. The technique has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods incorporating feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, establishing itself as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The technique addresses critical challenges in inference speed, memory footprint, and computational efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Principles, Applications, and Advances in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables efficient model deployment while maintaining performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks. Recent developments have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple logit matching to encompass feature-level transfer, adversarial training, and meta-learning frameworks, making it an increasingly versatile compression technique for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Model Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. The technique demonstrates significant effectiveness across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models with reduced computational footprints and latency. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple logit-matching to include sophisticated approaches such as attention-based mechanisms, intermediate layer alignment, multi-teacher strategies, and feature-level knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in computational overhead and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making it an essential paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks and improving model efficiency across multiple domains including computer vision and natural language processing. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing deployment challenges across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how neural networks are trained and deployed in practical real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized areas such as federated learning and graph neural networks, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, reducing computational and memory requirements while maintaining performance. This approach has been widely adopted across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with applications spanning from domain adaptation and multi-task learning to adversarial robustness and fair model compression. Recent advances have introduced task-aware filtering, attention-based feature matching, and progressive training strategies to improve the effectiveness of knowledge transfer and student model learning.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models, with methodologies ranging from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated multi-teacher frameworks and specialized approaches. The techniques address fundamental challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, and practical deployment while preserving predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying efficient neural networks across diverse domains. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, lightweight student models while maintaining or improving performance. This synthesis examines the current state of knowledge distillation techniques, their applications to natural language processing and computer vision tasks, and recent innovations in multi-teacher frameworks and domain-specific approaches. The research demonstrates that knowledge distillation provides a flexible and practical solution for reducing computational costs and memory requirements in both discriminative and generative models, with particular success in transformer-based language models, neural machine translation, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables efficient model deployment while maintaining performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks. Recent developments have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple logit matching to encompass feature-level transfer, adversarial training, and meta-learning frameworks, making it an increasingly versatile compression technique for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for enabling the efficient deployment of neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, federated learning, and specialized tasks, demonstrating the broad applicability and importance of these techniques for practical AI system deployment.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for addressing the fundamental challenge of deploying large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation enables practical implementation of state-of-the-art deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This position paper argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a simple compression tool—it is an essential paradigm for modern machine learning deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable compact student networks to learn from larger, more powerful teacher models through knowledge transfer mechanisms, reducing computational and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and generative models, making these techniques fundamental to practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications. Researchers have developed numerous extensions and refinements to address challenges such as data availability constraints, adversarial robustness, and cross-modal knowledge transfer, with applications spanning from resource-constrained device deployment to federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient neural network training, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This paper surveys the current state of knowledge distillation research across multiple domains, examining its applications to language models, computer vision tasks, and federated learning scenarios. We discuss key methodological advances including intermediate layer distillation, feature-based matching approaches, and attention-based mechanisms for improved knowledge transfer. Furthermore, we explore how distillation addresses practical challenges such as domain adaptation, model heterogeneity, and resource constraints in edge computing environments. The evidence demonstrates that distillation remains a versatile and effective strategy for creating deployable, efficient models without substantial sacrifice in performance.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges in resource-constrained environments. Beyond basic model compression, knowledge distillation serves multiple purposes including improved generalization, better robustness, fairness improvements, and enhanced interpretability. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment across resource-constrained environments. The field has expanded to address diverse scenarios including data-free distillation, intermediate layer matching, and applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized domains. Despite widespread adoption, the mechanisms underlying knowledge distillation and optimal transfer strategies remain areas of active research.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned representations and knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods, making knowledge distillation essential for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance loss. This technique transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable in natural language processing, where modern pre-trained models like BERT impose significant computational burdens for inference. Beyond compression, distillation serves broader purposes including domain adaptation, heterogeneous federated learning, and improved model generalization. The versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation across diverse applications demonstrate its importance as a foundational technique in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective techniques for training compact, efficient neural networks without sacrificing performance. This approach enables smaller "student" models to learn from larger, high-capacity "teacher" models through knowledge transfer, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments including mobile devices and real-time applications. The technique's versatility has enabled successful applications across diverse domains from computer vision to natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for creating efficient neural networks that maintain high performance while reducing computational and storage requirements. These methods involve training compact student networks to emulate larger, more powerful teacher networks through knowledge transfer mechanisms. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, enabling the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.
