papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making knowledge distillation an essential strategy for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Approach to Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for compressing large, complex neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deep learning systems practical for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments. Distillation techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating both theoretical soundness and practical utility.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Pathway to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, and memory footprint across diverse applications in computer vision and natural language processing, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized areas such as federated learning and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include multi-teacher approaches, layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms, data-free contexts, and task-specific compression strategies. Beyond simple model compression, distillation offers broader benefits including robustness improvements, better generalization, fairness enhancements, and improved interpretability in the resulting student models.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large, compute-intensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern deep learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, making it an essential technique for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model performance and real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Model Compression and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher networks to compact student networks. Beyond traditional classification tasks, knowledge distillation demonstrates remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. The technique continues to evolve with innovations in feature matching, attention mechanisms, and integration with complementary compression methods, establishing it as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This paper argues that knowledge distillation enables the creation of efficient, deployable models without sacrificing performance through strategic knowledge transfer from larger teacher networks to compact student networks. Beyond traditional compression, knowledge distillation extends to specialized domains including continual learning, privacy-preserving applications, and task-specific adaptation, demonstrating its versatility and fundamental importance in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Strategic Transfer of Learning from Large to Small Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep neural networks across resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Through strategic knowledge transfer mechanisms, distillation techniques have proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. The success of these methods relies on sophisticated mechanisms for capturing and transferring both task-relevant information and feature representations. Modern distillation frameworks continue to evolve, incorporating adaptive weighting schemes, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and adversarial learning strategies to maximize compression efficiency while minimizing performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. The method has been widely adopted across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, serving multiple purposes beyond basic compression including fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced model interpretability. Recent research reveals that distillation functions not only through explicit knowledge transfer but also as a form of learned regularization, with theoretical analyses providing deeper understanding of its mechanisms and benefits.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has become increasingly essential for deploying state-of-the-art models across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, addressing the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents the most practical and effective approach to model compression across deep learning and natural language processing applications. By enabling strategic knowledge transfer from teacher models to student models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size, computational requirements, and memory footprint while preserving the learned capabilities essential for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with innovations in training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific optimizations. The technique simultaneously reduces computational complexity, enables privacy-preserving model transfer, and improves model interpretability, establishing it as a fundamental paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. Recent advances extend the methodology beyond simple output matching to encompass feature-level transfer, zero-shot approaches, and application-specific strategies, making knowledge distillation essential for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques that enable the deployment of large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, these methods maintain competitive performance while dramatically reducing computational requirements and memory footprint. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential approach for practical AI deployment across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the fundamental tension between model capability and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for enabling the efficient deployment of sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches involve transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining competitive performance while dramatically reducing inference time and memory requirements. Knowledge distillation has proven versatile across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, establishing itself as an essential methodology for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation represents a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique addresses critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency, establishing it as an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Efficient Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a paradigm shift in how we approach model efficiency, offering practical solutions to the challenges of modern deep learning deployment, from NLP systems to computer vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an indispensable paradigm for making advanced neural networks accessible to real-world applications where deployment constraints are significant.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures, making it particularly valuable for NLP and deep learning applications where computational efficiency is essential. By examining diverse applications across multiple domains, this paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental solution to the practical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining high performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a large, well-trained teacher network to a smaller student network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, healthcare, and recommendation systems, addressing key challenges of inference latency, computational efficiency, and model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in computational overhead and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making it an essential paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to smaller, more deployable architectures across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. By enabling the deployment of high-performance models in resource-constrained environments, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in practical deep learning applications while supporting various advanced objectives including robustness, fairness, and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-efficient student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, and memory requirements, making it essential infrastructure for real-world deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This training approach transfers knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses advanced mechanisms such as intermediate layer alignment, attention-based transfer, feature-level matching, and adversarial training frameworks, making it an increasingly versatile tool for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more deployable models. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a student model, enabling substantial reductions in computational cost and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, with emerging techniques addressing domain-specific challenges and data-free scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models at Scale
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective model compression technique that enables the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models through various distillation strategies. Research demonstrates that knowledge distillation not only reduces computational overhead and memory requirements but also improves the generalization capabilities of compressed models across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an indispensable technique for deploying sophisticated deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental approach to model compression and knowledge transfer, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across diverse applications. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Recent advances have expanded the scope of distillation beyond traditional supervised learning to encompass task-aware filtering, multi-view learning, and data-free approaches, establishing it as a core technique in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Crucial Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a vital technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach spans multiple domains including natural language processing, speech processing, graph neural networks, and computer vision, offering flexible solutions for various model compression scenarios from standard settings to data-free contexts.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the practical deployment of advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The methodology has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and specialized applications, offering systematic solutions for reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient neural network training, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This paper surveys the current state of knowledge distillation research across multiple domains, examining its applications to language models, computer vision tasks, and federated learning scenarios. We discuss key methodological advances including intermediate layer distillation, feature-based matching approaches, and attention-based mechanisms for improved knowledge transfer. Furthermore, we explore how distillation addresses practical challenges such as domain adaptation, model heterogeneity, and resource constraints in edge computing environments. The evidence demonstrates that distillation remains a versatile and effective strategy for creating deployable, efficient models without substantial sacrifice in performance.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has become increasingly essential for deploying state-of-the-art models across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, addressing the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.
